items.title: Presidency announces 355 civil awards on Independence Day
items.description: ISLAMABAD: President Asif Ali Zardari on Friday approved several summaries sent by the prime minister, including the conferment of military and civil awards and a special remission of sentences for eligible prisoners. According to the Presidency, President Zardari approved military awards for 1,172 personnel of the armed forces and civil armed forces in recognition of their services. In addition, the president approved the conferment of national civil awards on 355 individuals on the occasion of the country’s Independence Day, honouring achievement across science, engineering, education, medicine, the arts, literature, sports, journalism, social welfare, philanthropy and public service, alongside a large slate of gallantry decorations dominated by personnel of the Federal Constabulary who were killed in the line of duty. The awards, announced on August 14, will be formally conferred at an investiture ceremony on Pakistan Day, March 23. Nishan-i-Pakistan The country’s highest civil award for a foreign national goes to Sheikha Fatima bint Mubarak, Supreme Chairwoman of the Family Development Foundation, United Arab Emirates. Nishan-i-Quaid-i-Azam Two physicians who attended to the founder of Pakistan, Dr Jal Rattanji Patel (Late) and Dr Jal Daeboo (Late), are recognised more than seven decades on. Nishan-i-Imtiaz Six government figures and one literary personality will be conferred the award: poet and writer Asad Muhammad Khan, Ishaq Dar, Mohsin Naqvi, Muhammad Aurangzeb, Ahad Khan Cheema, Bilal Azhar Kayani and the late Austro-Hungarian Muslim scholar Muhammad Asad (Late). Hilal-i-Pakistan Six foreign dignitaries were recognised for their services to Pakistan: Prince Saud bin Nayef bin Abdulaziz Al-Saud, Yousef bin Abdullah Al-Benyan, Mohammed Al-Tuwaijri, Deemah Al Yahya, Russian Deputy PM Alexey Logvinovich Overchuk, and Hiroji Kataoka. Hilal-i-Quaid-i-Azam The award went to Carey Schofield, an educationist working in Chitral. Sitara-i-Pakistan Three Turkish ministers and a Spanish senator were honoured: Hakan Fidan, Yasar Gular, Omer Bolat and Senator Vicente Azpitarte. Sitara-i-Quaid-i-Azam The award went to six recipients drawn from China, Spain, France and Malaysia. They included Yang Baoning of the China Academy of Space Technology, Master Yuan Xikun, Professor Zhou Yushu, Antonio Gutierrez Limones, Pascal Allizard, and Dr Maszlee bin Malik. Hilal-i-Imtiaz The award was conferred on fifteen recipients across the realms of technology, higher education, medicine, broadcasting, letters, the senior bureaucracy and the diaspora. These included Interactive Group CEO Dr Shahid Mahmud, NUTECH Rector Lt Gen (r) Moazzam Ejaz, renowned transplant surgeon Dr Faisal Saud Dar, HUM Network’s Sultana Siddiqi, and poets Ejaz Rahim and Khurshid Ul Hasan Rizvi. Five senior public servants were also honoured, including DG IB Fuad Asadullah, AGP Mansoor Usman Awan, Finance Secretary Imdadullah Bosal, FBR chief Rashid Mahmood Lagrial, and Establishment Secretary Barrister Nabeel A. Awan. The remaining awards went under the services to Pakistan head to Saudi Assistant Minister for Investment Ibrahim Al-Mubarak, and to three overseas Pakistanis: Dr Ghulam Murtaza in the UK, the late Prof Ahmed Ali in China, and Sardar Muhammad Ilyas Khan in Saudi Arabia. Sitara-i-Imtiaz In science and higher education, the award went to Kohat University of Science and Technology VC Prof Dr Syed Zafar Ilyas and Balochistan Public Service Commission member Prof Dr Mudassir Asrar, along with ICCBS Director and Unesco Chair Prof Dr Muhammad Raza Shah, FJMU Lahore VC Prof Dr Khalid Masood Gondal, PIDE VC Dr Rashid Amjad, and Taaleem Foundation founder Dr Zafar Iqbal Qadir. Two of the five medical awards are posthumous, going to bone marrow transplantation pioneer Prof Dr Tahir Shamsi (Late) and infectious diseases specialist Dr Naseem Salahuddin (Late). The others went to SICHN Executive Director Prof Dr Syed Jamal Raza, Battagram neurosurgeon Dr Shah Khalid, and physician Prof Dr Muhammad Khurram. Ten artists were recognised: actor Balqees Bano (Nisho Begum), comedian Iftikhar Ahmed Thakur, naat khawan Syed Fasih Uddin Soharwardhy, composer and compere Shakir Hussain, singer Taranam Naz, Sufi opera singer Saira John Peter, the late painter and art historian Abida Ehsan (posthumously), painter Raja Changez Sultan, theatre and TV artist Muhammad Naeem Tahir, and miniature painter Bashir Ahmed. In literature, the award went to short story writer Shakeel Adilzada, Iqbal scholar Prof Brig (r) Waheed Uz Zaman Tariq, poet Maqsood Hussain Jafri, naat writer Riaz ul Haq Tahir Riaz Majeed, writer Muhammad Hafeez Khan, historian Prof Dr Muhammad Saleem Mazhar, novelist Hashim Nadeem, and poet Syed Ghulam Abbas (Muhsin Naqvi). Boxing coach Atta Mohammad Kakar and martial artist and yoga pioneer Dr Waseem A Tai were honoured in sports, journalists Muhammad Saleh Zaafir and Haji Nawaz Raza in journalism, WHO technical officer Dr Maryam Mallick and Nayyab Ali in social welfare, and Shanawar Khan in philanthropy. Twenty-eight public servants also received the Sitara-i-Imtiaz, while under gallantry and public service, the award went to Ahmad Arifeen and to three Punjab police officers recognised for the Kacha operation — IGP Abdul Kareem, DIG Waqas Hassan and DIG Tanveer Hussain Tunio. Danish citizen of Pakistani origin Justice Muhammad Ahsan and UAE-based Haji Khan Zaman Saroor were honoured for services to Pakistan. Tamgha-i-Imtiaz The Tamgha-i-Imtiaz is the largest single category on the list. In science, it went to One Health and AMR focal person Dr Sajjad Hussain, PIEAS Deputy Chief Scientist Prof Dr Aneela Zameer Jaffery and GIS specialist Dr Urooj Saeed, and in engineering to UET Peshawar VC Dr Muhammad Sadiq and PIEAS Principal Engineer Prof Dr Naeem-ul-Haq Tariq. Sixteen educationists were honoured: Women University Mardan and Swabi VC Prof Dr Ghazala Yasmeen, AIOU VC Prof Dr Nasir Mahmood, LUMS Dean Prof Dr Faisal Bari, former LCWU VC Prof Dr Sabiha Mansoor, University of Loralai VC Prof Engr Dr Ehsan Ullah Kakar, IBCC chief Dr Ghulam Ali Mallah, TCF’s Riaz Ahmed Kamlani, retired FDE principals Sabah Faisal and Muhammad Rafique Malik, Cambridge Advisors Network co-founder Syed Azhar Afaq Rizvi, former Sindh High Court judge Qazi Khalid Ali, Diamer-Astore Education Director Faqir Ullah, Abdul Sattar, researcher Dr Ruhi Khalid, CPSP fellow supervisor Prof Dr Sardar Muhammad Ali Ayaz Sadiq, and educationist and philanthropist Yasmeen Dadabhai. In medicine, the award went to CDA Hospital surgery head Dr Naeem Taj, Quetta cardiac surgeon Dr Abdul Wasay, Hashmanis Group chairman Dr Mohammad Sharif Hashmani, and bariatric and laparoscopic surgeon Dr Maaz Ul Hassan. Twelve artists were recognised: actor and anchor Noor Ul Hassan Malik, host Shafat Ali, singer and composer Shiraz Uppal, singer Jabbar Abbas, painter Ali Saad, khussa maker Muhammad Ramzan, shoemaker Jahangir Khan, stone carver Ghulam Haider, Balochi chawat maker Rozi Khan, naat khawans Akhtar Qureshi and Khan Muhammad Chachar, and fashion designer Rubina Kazmi. Ten literary figures were honoured: writer Farida Hafeez, novelist Agha Gul, writer Noor Khan Muhammad Hasni, writer and translator Khalid Fateh Muhammad, poet Haleem Qureshi, writers Manzoom Ali and Sherbaz Ali Khan Barcha, the late historian and archaeologist Muhammad Siddique G Memon (posthumously), Iqbal scholar Prof Dr Haroon-ur-Rasheed Tabassum, and author Qaiser Abbas Sabir. Athlete Faiqa Riaz was the sole sports recipient. Seven journalists were recognised — Muhammad Riaz Khan, culture journalist Shoaib Ahmed, Ammar Masood, news anchors Dr Maria Zulfiqar, Adil Shahzaib and Hammad Hassan, and Tasawwar Arafat. Religious scholars Qari Rooh Ullah Madani, Hafiz Asad Ubaid, Syed Riaz Hussain Najfi and Bishop Humphri Sarfraz Peters were honoured under social welfare, while Haripur Chamber of Commerce President Atif Ikram Sheikh, National Forum of Women with Disabilities Chairperson Abia Akram and Pakistan Association of the Blind President Riaz Hussain Memon were recognised for philanthropy. President’s Pride of Performance Forty-six people will receive the President’s Award for Pride of Performance, most of them from the performing and visual arts. Thirty arts recipients were named. Among the actors and directors are Mahmood Aslem, Sarfraz Hussain Ansari, M Ehtesham Warsi, Arshad Hussain, Ghazala Kaifi, Khawaja Saleem Ahmad, Shazma Haleem, Syeda Maria Wasti and Sania Saeed. From music, the award went to sarangi players Ustad Mazhar Umrao Bundu Khan and Zohaib Hassan, singer Rafia Bano, classical musician Jahangir Iqbal (Ustad Ejaz Tawakal Khan), BJS Qawwal Group’s Nadeem Salamat, harmonium soloist Shahbaz Ali, ghazal singer Gulshan Ara Syed, the late folk singer Talib Hussain Dard (posthumously), singers Mushtaq Shifai and Zulfiqar Jabbar Khan (Zulfi), and choreographers Shaukat Hussain Samrat (Pappu Samrat) and Syed Wahab Hussain Shah. In the visual arts and crafts, it went to painter and illustrator Aftab Zafar, painter and sculptor Tayyeba Aziz, artist Aleem Dad Khan, boreendo maker Allah Jurio, Kashmiri embroidery artist Sheikh Muhammad Yousaf, natural-dye block printer Ameer Buksh, painters Nasir Shahzad and Muhammad Imran Qureshi, and sculptor and cultural consultant Hidayat Ullah Khan. Eight literary figures were recognised: Dr Shahida Shaheen, Ali Muhammad Farshi, Aslam Javed, Muhammad Muti-Ur-Rehman Mumtaz (Rehman Faris), Syed Farid Ullah Shah Hassas, Shafqat Ullah Mushtaq, Nizakat Kalsoom (Kalsoom Zeb) and Syed Wasi Ahmad Fatmi. Six athletes made the list — wrestler Bashir Bhola, shooter Kishmala Talat, squash player Noor Zaman, ramp jumper Sultan Muhammad Golden, boxer Muhammad Waseem and cricketer Sadiq Muhammad — along with journalist Syed Hammad Ghaznavi and photojournalist Muhammad Amir Khan. Gallantry awards Security and law-enforcement personnel account for the single largest bloc on this year’s list, with 91 gallantry decorations approved in addition to the awards named above. Forty-eight were conferred Sitara-i-Shuja’at awards, 24 received the Tamgha-i-Shuja’at while 19 officials were awarded the Tamgha-i-Imtiaz for gallantry and public service. These are separate from the military awards for 1,172 serving personnel of the Armed Forces and Civil Armed Forces approved by the president on the same day. Published in Dawn, August 15th, 2026

items.title: Gas supply disruption persists in Balochistan as repair work awaits security clearance
items.description: QUETTA: Despite the passage of three days, repair work on the damaged gas pipeline could not begin as several cities and towns in Balochistan, including parts of the provincial capital, remained without gas supply on Friday. The 18-inch-diameter main gas pipeline was blown up by unidentified people using explosives in the Bolan riverbed in Kachhi district on Wednesday night, disrupting gas supplies to several districts of Balochistan. Officials said the relevant security authorities had yet to provide clearance for repair teams to enter the affected area and replace the damaged pipeline. Gas supply was suspended to several towns and cities, including parts of Quetta, after the main pipeline was blown up in the Bolan area of Kachhi district. Officials of the Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) confirmed the incident and said the pipeline had been badly damaged, disrupting gas supplies. “The explosion occurred at the KMP-246 valve assembly in the Bolan riverbed area near Gorkat, around 700 to 800 metres from the main Quetta-Sibi Road,” officials said, adding that it was an 18-inch-diameter pipeline. They said unidentified people had planted high explosives beneath the pipeline and detonated them using a remote control. Flames and smoke were seen rising from the damaged pipeline following the explosion. “After the pipeline explosion, gas supplies were suspended to Kolpur, Mach, Mastung, Kalat, Pishin, Ziarat and many parts of Quetta,” officials said, adding that consumers could face reduced gas pressure or disruption in supply. SSGC officials said repair teams were ready to begin work but were awaiting security clearance before entering the affected area. The teams would be dispatched to the site immediately after clearance was granted, the company said. Published in Dawn, August 15th, 2026

items.title: Chenab, Ravi nullahs may enter high flood category
items.description: LAHORE: The Flood Forecasting Division (FFD) of the Pakistan Meteorological Department has warned of possible high flooding in storm-water nullahs linked to the Chenab and Ravi rivers from Aug 15 to 21 as flows in these waterways continue to rise. The FFD said flows at major rim-gauging stations of the Chenab and Ravi were expected to remain at low flood levels during the period, while adjoining nullahs could experience low to medium flooding. However, a significant increase in flows in tributary nullahs could lead to high flood levels. It forecast no significant increase in inflows at major gauging stations of the Indus, Kabul, Jhelum, Ravi and Sutlej over the next 24 hours, although several stations could reach low flood levels. Flows at Taunsa, Marala, Khanki, Qadirabad and Sidhnai are expected to enter the low-flood range, while Tarbela, Kalabagh, Chashma, Guddu and Balloki are likely to remain at low flood levels. The FFD also warned of flash flooding in tributary streams of the Kabul River and hill torrents in the Dera Ghazi Khan division during the forecast period. Tarbela at maximum conservation level as Mangla 67pc full According to the FFD, Tarbela Dam, Kalabagh and Chashma on the Indus were experiencing low-level flooding on Friday evening, with flows of 268,200, 365,870 and 321,667 cusecs, respectively, recorded at 6pm on Aug 14. The department forecast widespread rain, wind and thunderstorms, with isolated heavy falls, over the upper catchments of all major rivers during the next 24 hours. The areas include Islamabad, Gilgit-Baltistan, Kashmir, upper Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and several districts of upper Punjab. The FFD said Tarbela reservoir had attained its maximum conservation level, while Mangla was yet to reach its maximum, with the reservoir 67 per cent full. Meanwhile, according to Wapda’s daily report for Aug 14, inflows and outflows at Tarbela were recorded at 274,100 and 273,300 cusecs, respectively. At Nowshera, inflows and outflows of the Kabul River were 32,700 cusecs each. The Jhelum at Mangla recorded inflows of 28,400 cusecs and outflows of 7,000 cusecs, while the Chenab at Marala had inflows of 81,000 cusecs and outflows of 62,000 cusecs. Tarbela Dam’s water level stood at 1,550 feet, its maximum conservation level, with live storage of 5.580 million acre-feet (MAF). Mangla’s level was 1,209.75 feet against its maximum conservation level of 1,242 feet, with live storage of 4.870 MAF. Chashma lake was at 648.50 feet, just half a foot below its maximum conservation level of 649 feet, with live storage of 0.285 MAF. Wapda said the inflows and outflows at Tarbela, Jinnah and Chashma, the Kabul at Nowshera and the Jhelum at Mangla were reported as 24-hour mean flows. Published in Dawn, August 15th, 2026

items.title: Galamsey: ‘Challenge is prosecution, not arrest’ — Lands Minister
items.description: The government’s intensified campaign against illegal mining (galamsey) has resulted in the arrest of 258 suspects and the seizure or immobilisation of thousands of pieces of mining equipment, but the prosecution of those arrested remains a major concern. The Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, said the effectiveness of the anti-galamsey campaign could not be measured by arrests and seizures alone, stressing the need to ensure that cases reach their logical conclusion in court. “The challenge we are having is not the arrest. It is the prosecution.” Mr Buah made the disclosure at a policy engagement with the IMANI Centre for Policy and Education in Accra on Thursday, August 13, where he discussed the challenges inherited by the government, ongoing reforms and measures being implemented to address illegal mining. 258 arrested According to the minister, 258 suspects had been arrested in operations targeting illegal mining in forest reserves as of July 2026. However, the Ministry did not provide a corresponding breakdown of how many of the suspects had been charged, prosecuted or convicted, or how many cases remained pending. Mr Buah said the ministry was working with the Attorney-General’s Department to address the difficulties associated with prosecuting illegal mining cases. The issue puts the spotlight on the justice component of the government’s anti-galamsey drive, particularly whether enforcement operations can produce lasting results if arrests do not translate into successful prosecutions and convictions. The Ministry’s enforcement figures show that 200 excavators had been seized and 34 immobilised by July 2026. The authorities had also seized 1,469 pumping machines, 950 changfan machines, 48 tricycles, 285 motorbikes and 82 gold detectors. A further 1,259 pumping machines and 774 changfan machines had been immobilised, while 801 structures had also been immobilised during operations in forest reserves. 8,900 hectares degraded Mr Buah also disclosed that approximately 8,900 hectares of forest reserves had been completely degraded through illegal mining and other destructive activities. Nine forest reserves were identified as among the worst affected. According to the minister, some of the affected areas had become difficult for Forestry Commission officials to access because of the activities of illegal miners, including the reported presence of weapons and incidents of violence. He said previous assessments had underestimated the extent of the damage because they were based on older data. The restoration of the degraded areas, he added, would require substantial resources. 4,000 excavators held at ports As part of efforts to prevent excavators from being diverted into illegal mining operations, the government has introduced tighter controls on the importation and deployment of the machines. Mr Buah said more than 4,000 excavators were being held at the country’s ports pending compliance with a new documentation and clearance regime. Under the arrangement, importers are required to provide information on the importer, intended end user and location where each excavator will be deployed before clearance. The Minerals Commission has established a presence at the ports to facilitate the process. Approved excavators are expected to be fitted with tracking devices and monitored through geofencing to ensure that they operate only within their declared locations. The government’s stated objective is to make excavators operating in Ghana traceable. Focus shifts to galamsey supply chain The government is also seeking to disrupt the supply chain that supports illegal mining. Mr Buah said 1,724 of the machines seized or immobilised were changfans, many of which were fabricated locally before being transported to mining areas and water bodies. The development has raised concerns about the role of local manufacturers, suppliers and financiers in sustaining illegal mining operations. The government has also deployed about 2,000 Blue Water Guards to provide community-based intelligence and support first-response efforts around affected water bodies. Mr Buah, however, acknowledged concerns over discipline within the initiative, including allegations that some guards had accepted bribes. He maintained that the programme had nevertheless provided useful support to enforcement efforts. Mining licensing reforms The government is also pursuing changes to the mining licensing regime as part of its broader response to challenges within the sector. Mr Buah said the proposed reforms would reduce the maximum initial duration of large-scale mining leases from 30 years to 20 years. The Ministry also plans to introduce stricter requirements for holders of exploration and prospecting licences to demonstrate meaningful activity within specified periods. Mr Buah criticised situations in which companies retain mining concessions for extended periods without undertaking significant exploration or development. Another proposal is the establishment of district mining committees to give communities a greater role in mining-related decisions. The committees would, among other things, consider the potential impact of proposed mining operations on water bodies, farms and settlements before licences are approved. Mining companies would also be required to enter into community development agreements to define their responsibilities towards communities hosting mining operations. The figures presented by the Lands Ministry highlight the scale of the government’s enforcement operations, but the prosecution of suspects remains a critical measure of their effectiveness. With 258 arrests, hundreds of machines seized or immobilised and thousands of hectares of forest reserves affected, the ability of the state to successfully prosecute offenders could determine whether the current enforcement campaign produces a sustained deterrent against illegal mining.

items.title: Govt raises petroleum dealers’ margin to Rs9.98 per litre
items.description: • PPDA calls off nationwide strike planned from today • Higher margin to take effect from Sept 1 ISLAMABAD: In a move aimed at averting a nationwide strike by petroleum dealers, the Economic Coordination Com­mittee (ECC) of the federal cabinet on Friday approved a 15.5 per cent increase in dealers’ margins on both petrol and high-speed diesel, following which the dealers called off their protest planned from Saturday. The decision raises the dealers’ margin on both fuels by Rs1.34 per litre, from Rs8.64 to Rs9.98 per litre. The revised margin is scheduled to take effect from Sept 1. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb chaired the ECC meeting virtually, while Finance Secretary Imdadullah Bosal attended in person at the Finance Division. The meeting was convened on a public holiday after petroleum dealers announced a nationwide strike from Aug 15, prompting the government to take up the matter on an urgent basis. The Finance Division’s statement did not disclose the exact increase in dealers’ margins. However, officials confirmed that the ECC had approved the proposal submitted by the Petroleum Division. “Yes, the ECC approved the same increase proposed by the Petroleum Division,” a senior official privy to the meeting told Dawn . According to the summary submitted to the ECC, the dealers’ margin was proposed to be increased by Rs1.34 per litre to Rs9.98. Soon after the decision, the Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association (PPDA) called off its plan to launch a nationwide strike from Saturday. The association had earlier given the federal government a 72-hour ultimatum , accusing it of failing to honour assurances made by the petroleum minister regarding its demands. The dealers had sought replacement of the existing fixed margin with a variable margin linked to the retail prices of petrol and diesel, proposing that it be set at 8pc of the retail price of both fuels. According to official sources, acceptance of that demand would have raised the dealers’ margin to around Rs26 per litre on petrol and Rs30 per litre on diesel at current retail prices, resulting in a substantially higher burden on consumers. The ECC instead approved the 15.51pc increase in the fixed margin. The margin of oil marketing companies (OMCs) remains unchanged at Rs7.87 per litre on both petrol and diesel. A proposal to increase the OMC margin by Rs1.22 per litre remains linked to the implementation of digitisation measures. An official Finance Division statement said the ECC considered a summary submitted by the Petroleum Division and deliberated on the revision of dealers’ margins on motor spirit and high-speed diesel (HSD). In December 2025, the ECC had approved an increase of Rs2.56 per litre in dealers’ margins on petrol and diesel. The decision was subsequently modified by the federal cabinet, prompting the PPDA to demand its implementation. The shift from fortnightly to daily petroleum price revisions added another demand from dealers, who sought to link their margins to retail prices. The government, however, decided to retain the daily pricing mechanism. Under the ECC’s December 2025 decision, 50pc of the proposed increase was to take effect from Dec 15, subject to a declining trend in petroleum prices, while the remaining 50pc was linked to achievement of digitisation targets set by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra). On Dec 23, the federal cabinet modified the decision, making the increase conditional on completion of digitisation targets by OMCs and petroleum dealers. With the digitisation drive still under way, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik held a meeting on July 22 with representatives of the All Pakistan Petrol Pump Owners Association and the PPDA following an earlier strike call. Senior Petroleum Division officials and the Ogra chairman also attended. The dealers urged the government to delink the increase in their margins from digitisation, arguing that implementation of the initiative was primarily the responsibility of OMCs. They also reiterated their demand that the fixed margin of Rs8.64 per litre be replaced with a margin equivalent to 8pc of the retail price of petrol and diesel. Published in Dawn, August 15th, 2026

items.title: New administrative units ‘under serious consideration’
items.description: • Top govt functionary thinks discussion could be precursor to proposed 28th Constitutional Amendment • Proposals include bringing Karachi, Gwadar under federal control; splitting Punjab into three, KP into two units ISLAMABAD: There is a serious debate underway in power corridors over the most feasible approach to creating new provinces, according to a top government functionary, who thinks the discussion is a precursor to the proposed 28th Constitutional Amendment . The government source, who is privy to developments, was reluctant to say when the proposal — still said to be in the initial stages — could materialise. He conceded, however, that turning the idea of new administrative into reality would not be easy, as building a consensus among major political parties, which appear opposed to the idea, would be a major challenge. The functionary said discussions were focused on whether new provinces should be created and, if so, how many would suffice; whether more administrative units should instead be established; or whether the local government system should be revived and empowered. According to the source, the most effective way to address the consequences of the 18th Amendment was to create new provinces. He said this could help resolve many of the problems faced by the federal government following the devolution of powers to the provinces. Recently, while addressing the Pakistan Economic Summit 2026, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi urged all political parties to resolve key national issues, including the creation of new provinces, describing it as the only solution to improving the country’s overall condition, which he said had “collapsed”. The issue gained momentum after the minister’s proposal drew strong reactions from government ministers, while the country’s leading lawyers’ bodies adopted divergent positions . The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) backed the proposal, whereas the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC) stressed that any such move must be pursued strictly within the constitutional fram­ework, through parliament and with national consensus. Speaking at a Full Court Reference held at the Supreme Court in honour of Justice Musarrat Hilali on her retirement, SCBA President Haroonur Rashid said the association endorsed and supported the proposal to create new provinces. He said the SCBA believed that any constitutional measure to create additional provinces would promote better governance through devolution and equitable administration at the grassroots level, create equal opportunities for balanced economic development and strengthen political stability. The creation of more provinces, he added, would also help improve living standards by addressing the economic hardships faced by people. The PBC, the apex representative body of the legal fraternity, meanwhile, said at its 250th meeting that all constitutional matters must be addressed strictly within the framework of the Constitution. How many more? The government functionary said that if it was ultimately decided that creating more provinces was the only solution to what the interior minister had described as a “collapsing system”, the next question would be how many provinces should be created. Under one proposal being discussed, he said, Karachi and Gwadar could come under the administrative control of the federal government, while the rest of Sindh would remain a single province. Similarly, Balochistan could be divided into two provinces, while Punjab could be divided into three. Khyber Pakhtun­khwa, however, presents a more complicated case beca­use of the merger of the erstwhile Federally Administered Tribal Areas (Fata) and the inco­rporation of areas previously administered under the Fata and Pata arrangements into the provincial constitutional, legal and judicial framework. The source said KP could nevertheless be divided into Pakhtun and Hazara regions. Stronger local govt Alternatively, he said, if the decision was taken to strengthen the local government system, funds for local governments could be channelled directly through the federal government instead of the provinces. Had the local government system introduced during the late President Pervez Musharraf’s tenure continued uninterrupted, he said, a large pool of experienced and competent councillors would have been available to address local issues effectively. “Unfortunately, reaching that level of experience and building such a team will now take considerable time,” he added. Published in Dawn, August 15th, 2026

items.title: Containers to stay off roads as transporters remain divided
items.description: • Pakistan Transport Council ‘calls off’ wheel-jam after government accepts their eight demands • Oil tankers association also dissociates itself from strike after Ogra agrees to terms ISLAMABAD: A section of goods transporters on Friday called off its nationwide wheel-jam strike after reaching an agreement with the government, but major operators comprising container trailers, trucks and edible oil tankers remained off the roads, prolonging disruption to port operations and the country’s external trade. Meanwhile, fuel oil tankers dissociated themselves from the strike after the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) accepted their key demands. Oil Tankers Contractors Asso­ciation General Secretary Malik Shoaib Ashraf told Dawn that oil tankers were not part of the strike as their demands had been acce­pted by Ogra and a notification regarding an increase in freight charges was expected next week. “The freight charges are adjusted after every two years, but it has been delayed for three years this time. An increase of 7-8 per cent is expected next week,” Mr Ashraf said. Meanwhile, the Pakistan Transport Council, a constituent of the All Pakistan Goods Transporters Alliance, announced that it had called off the nationwide strike following what it described as successful negotiations with the government. Addressing a press conference at the National Press Club, council office-bearers said movement of their goods carriers was being restored across the country. The press conference was attended by Central President Tanveer Ahmed Jutt, Patron Muhammad Altaf, Founder Rao Tahir Khan, Central Vice President Ashraf Gujjar and other office-bearers. The council leadership said goods transportation operations from Karachi Port and Port Qasim were also being restored with immediate effect. They said a special committee formed by the prime minister and headed by Communications Minister Abdul Aleem Khan had held negotiations with the transporters. As a result, eight of the transporters’ immediate demands had been accepted, while committees had been constituted to address the remaining issues. The council said the agreement with the government carried the signatures of office-bearers representing 15 goods transport associations from across the country. Among their demands were no increase in toll taxes for one year, removal of additional toll plazas and implementation of a modern automated system. The council leadership also said an agreement had been reached for the immediate release, against bank guarantees, of vehicles detained under SRO 1619. The committees established to address other long-standing issues would remain in contact with the relevant government institutions, they added. However, All Pakistan Goods Transport Owners Association President Muhammad Owais Choudhry said only one segment of the All Pakistan Goods Transporters Alliance had broken ranks and that the strike by container trailers and trucks would continue as their key demands had not been met. He said the strike, which had continued for the past six days, was adversely affecting port activities. “The smaller goods carrier vehicles have called off the strike, but the large vehicles that move between provinces and carry heavy loads are still off the roads,” Mr Choudhry said. “The government is playing politics with us — buying time under the garb of negotiations while threatening our members through other means,” he alleged. Edible oil tankers also remained on strike. Edible Oil Contractors Association President Tariq Sarbaz said operators were not lifting palm oil and palm olein from the ports for transportation to oil factories. He said the best way out of the crisis was for the government to accept the transporters’ legitimate demands. Another meeting between the government and the striking transporters is scheduled to be held at the communications ministry on Saturday morning. Published in Dawn, August 15th, 2026

items.title: Trump signals plan to claim Hormuz ‘soon’
items.description: • Urges Americans to accept higher gas prices to stop Iran going nuclear • UAE accuses Tehran of attacking two vessels; shipping in the strait comes to near standstill • Riyadh, Abu Dhabi, Doha condemn strikes, demand unconditional return to free navigation • Houthis strike Saudi oil site, Yemen’s Mocha port; eight killed • JD Vance confirms keeping US energy prices down is ‘goal number one’; Bessent vows sanctions ‘world has never seen’ against Tehran GARDEN CITY: US President Donald Trump said on Friday that he would “soon” declare the strategic Strait of Hormuz a US territory once Iran is defeated, even as fresh attacks on Emirati oil tankers brought maritime traffic in the vital waterway to a near standstill. Trump’s remarks at a New York rally underscored the escalating international struggle over the narrow corridor, where a grinding stalemate of retaliatory blockades has shifted Washington’s immediate wartime focus from containing Iran’s nuclear programme to preventing an energy crisis that could hit Americans at the pump. “After we finish defeating Iran, which is being very badly defeated — pretty soon I’ll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States,” Trump said with a chuckle during an appearance at a police academy in New York state. “It’s true.” “We have the blockade. No ships get through unless we want them to,” Trump told a cheering crowd of supporters and police. He urged Americans to accept slightly higher gasoline prices as the cost of preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. Trump said Americans who had to “pay a tiny little bit more for your gasoline” should remember that this was the cost of ensuring “a very evil country” could not have a nuclear weapon. “What we’re doing is a great service for the world, not only for ourselves … and we’re really doing a great job,” said Trump, adding he would never apologise for attacking Iran. Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates accused Iran on Friday of attacking two state-owned commercial vessels transiting the strategic waterway. The UAE foreign ministry condemned what it described as a “hostile Iranian attack” on two vessels affiliated with the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC), saying there were no injuries. ADNOC confirmed the vessels had been attacked on Thursday evening but said the incidents had been brought under control, according to the state news agency WAM . Britain’s United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations later reported two nearly identical drone strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, causing minor damage. The incidents came just days after ADNOC said three of its tankers had also been attacked in the same waterway. The latest attacks appeared to have an immediate impact on shipping. Vessel-tracking data from Kpler suggested traffic through the strait had slowed dramatically on Friday, with only two non-oil vessels passing through and no crude shipments visible. With commercial transit severely disrupted, the United States vowed to maintain an indefinite naval blockade of Iranian ports and unleash historic economic pressure on Tehran. “Indefinitely the United States Navy can maintain a blockade like that because we’ll rotate ships in and out, as we have, and we’ll continue to,” US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth told reporters during a trip to Panama. Iran, meanwhile, has sought to use the strait as its strongest bargaining chip. By disrupting commercial shipping and threatening global oil supplies, Tehran has shifted the conflict from the battlefield to the world’s energy markets. “Alongside the threat to energy infrastructure in the region, Iran’s ability to restrict shipping through the strait is its main source of leverage in negotiations,” said Torbjorn Solvedt, principal Middle East analyst with risk intelligence company Verisk Maplecroft. That leverage was reflected in unusually candid remarks from Vice-President JD Vance, who acknowledged that keeping fuel prices low had overtaken Iran’s nuclear ambitions as Washington’s most immediate concern. “I know that oil is down today and it’s way down from the highs in the early days of the conflict,” Vance said on Fox News . “That’s goal number one — keep oil and gas cheap for Americans all over our country. And then obviously goal number two is ensure that Iran never gets a nuclear weapon.” Meanwhile, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the United States planned to inflict more financial damage on Iran, threatening to subject Tehran to economic isolation “like the world has never seen before”. “Watch this space for more announcements next week because we are going to apply measures like have never been seen in the history of economic isolation of a country,” he said in an interview. The remarks underscored how dramatically the conflict has evolved. What began as a campaign centred on preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon — consistently touted by President Donald Trump as his main reason for the war — has become a struggle over control of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow maritime corridor through which roughly a fifth of the world’s oil supply normally passes. Iran has imposed an effective blockade of the strait, frequently attacking commercial ships, and wants to charge users for passage, which the US fiercely opposes. The US military reportedly burnt through stockpiles of costly high-tech missiles and other weapons in the months since the war started at a cost of billions and is now reportedly running low, limiting Trump’s options for resuming attacks on Iran. Meanwhile, Trump struggles to find a way out of the war and shies away from resuming large-scale attacks. The 80-year-old president’s approval rating is plummeting, the war is unpopular among Americans, and midterm elections are approaching in November. Republicans fear Trump and the war, which has caused gasoline prices to soar, will cost them their control of Congress. Only days ago Trump had said an agreement to reopen the strait was imminent. Now his administration seems to be digging in, with diplomacy on hold as he hopes economic suffering will cause Iran to yield. Regional powers condemned the latest attacks. Saudi Arabia denounced the targeting of two oil tankers belonging to the United Arab Emirates’ Abu Dhabi National Oil Company in the Strait of Hormuz. In a statement, Riyadh’s foreign ministry said the attacks constitute “an unacceptable recurrence of Iranian attacks targeting commercial vessels and tankers”. “The kingdom holds Iran fully responsible for the consequences of persisting in these attacks, demanding an immediate halt to these violations and adherence to relevant international laws,” the statement added. Qatar also strongly condemned an “Iranian attack” targeting two Emirati oil tankers belonging to ADNOC which were crossing the Strait of Hormuz, deeming it “a severe violation of international law, the freedom of maritime navigation, and a clear violation of UN Security Council resolution 2817”. In a statement, the foreign ministry reiterated Doha’s “firm rejection of using the Strait of Hormuz as leverage”, demanding that it be opened unconditionally. The regional conflict showed little sign of easing elsewhere. In Yemen, the country’s internationally recognised government said the Houthis fired six ballistic missiles at the Red Sea port of Mocha on Friday, killing eight people in an attack it said targeted civilian infrastructure and national assets. The Houthis, for their part, said they had targeted what they described as Saudi-backed military build-ups, weapons depots and warships belonging to Saudi-backed forces and “mercenaries” in Mocha with a barrage of ballistic missiles, claiming to have destroyed boats and military equipment. The group also said it had carried out a separate cross-border attack. The Houthi-run SABA news agency quoted a military source as saying the rebels had targeted an Aramco facility in the Saudi city of Najran with a drone. The source said the strike was in response to what it described as Saudi military aircraft entering airspace over the northeastern part of Yemen’s Saada governorate. It did not identify the specific facility targeted or say whether it had been hit. There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi authorities or Aramco. Published in Dawn, August 15th, 2026

items.title: Pape Thiaw réclame plus de 423 millions FCFA à la Fédération sénégalaise de football
items.description: L’ancien sélectionneur de l’équipe nationale du Sénégal, Pape Bouna Thiaw, réclame à la Fédération sénégalaise de football (FSF) le paiement d’une somme de 423.820.300 FCFA. Par l’intermédiaire de son avocat, le technicien sénégalais a adressé une mise en demeure à l’instance dirigeante du football national. Cette démarche intervient sur fond de différend financier entre les deux parties. Dans le document adressé à la FSF, Pape Thiaw fait état de plusieurs sommes qu’il estime lui être dues au titre de ses fonctions et des différentes échéances sportives auxquelles il a participé avec les Lions. Salaires, primes et indemnités au cœur de la réclamation Le montant réclamé englobe plusieurs rubriques. Il comprend notamment des salaires impayés, des primes, des indemnités de logement et de déplacement, mais également des sommes liées aux performances de l’équipe nationale. Parmi les éléments mentionnés figurent notamment les primes relatives à la Coupe d’Afrique des nations (CAN) ainsi que celles liées à la qualification du Sénégal pour la prochaine Coupe du monde. Au total, la réclamation porte donc sur 423 millions 820 mille 300 FCFA, une somme conséquente qui place désormais la FSF face à une demande formelle de règlement. Une mise en demeure avant une éventuelle procédure À travers cette mise en demeure, l’avocat de Pape Thiaw invite la Fédération sénégalaise de football à procéder au règlement des sommes réclamées dans les meilleurs délais. À défaut d’un règlement ou d’un accord entre les deux parties, le dossier pourrait prendre une tournure judiciaire. La mise en demeure constitue ainsi une étape préalable avant l’éventuelle saisine des juridictions compétentes. Pour l’heure, aucune réaction officielle de la FSF sur cette réclamation n’a été communiquée. Cheikh Gora DIOP

items.description: Un réseau de trafic de drogue a utilisé un véhicule arborant les logos d'une association caritative venant en aide aux orphelins et aux familles dans le besoin pour transporter une cargaison de drogue et éviter d'éveiller les soupçons, avant d'être intercepté par les forces de la gendarmerie à Akjoujt. La gendarmerie a indiqué aujourd’hui dans un communiqué que la compagnie d’Akjoujt, en coordination avec la compagnie n° 1 de Nouakchott et le groupe n° 1 d’intervention rapide, de surveillance et d’intervention, avait saisi 77,055 kg de résine de cannabis transformée, connue sous le nom de « pierre noire », et arrêté dix personnes soupçonnées d’être liées au réseau. Elle a ajouté que l’enquête avait révélé que le véhicule servait de couverture pour faciliter le transport de la cargaison et éviter d’éveiller les soupçons. Cette opération est la dernière d’une série d’opérations de sécurité annoncées récemment par la Gendarmerie nationale. Depuis début juillet, ses unités ont ainsi réussi à démanteler plus de 15 réseaux actifs dans le trafic de stupéfiants et de substances psychotropes, selon une synthèse des données publiées par l’organisme. Ces opérations ont abouti à l’arrestation d’au moins 40 personnes et à la saisie de plus de 20 kilogrammes de stupéfiants de différentes sortes, ainsi que de plus de 10 000 comprimés de substances psychotropes et de pilules hallucinogènes.

items.title: Patrouilles conjointes mauritano-sénégalaises le long du fleuve pour lutter contre les activités illégales
items.description: Les forces de défense et de sécurité sénégalaises et mauritaniennes ont lancé jeudi des patrouilles fluviales conjointes le long de la frontière entre les deux pays, dans le cadre du renforcement de la surveillance de la zone frontalière et de la lutte contre les activités illégales. Participent à cette opération des unités de la deuxième région militaire sénégalaise, appuyées par des unités mauritaniennes, ainsi que des bateaux de la marine et des éléments de la police et de la gendarmerie des deux pays. Au cours de cette première journée, les équipes conjointes ont parcouru plusieurs secteurs frontaliers, notamment les zones de Tasim et de Senthiani Diama, où elles ont mené des opérations de surveillance et de suivi de la situation le long de la frontière. Ces patrouilles s’inscrivent dans le cadre de la coopération sécuritaire et militaire entre Nouakchott et Dakar, et visent à renforcer la coordination entre les forces des deux pays et à améliorer la surveillance des frontières communes, contribuant ainsi à la prévention des activités illégales. Cette opération vise également à rassurer les populations résidant dans les zones frontalières et à renforcer la coopération sur le terrain entre les forces de sécurité et les forces armées des deux pays. La Mauritanie et le Sénégal organisent régulièrement des patrouilles conjointes dans la zone frontalière, dans le but de renforcer la coordination en matière de sécurité et la surveillance des frontières communes.

Après une journée de vote le 13 août où Les Zambiens ont voté pour élire leur président et leurs députés, des tensions ont éclaté ce vendredi 14 août pendant la compilation des résultats. items.title: Une association étudiante critique la réduction du nombre de filières et celui des places en master et réclame leur augmentation
items.description: L'Union nationale des étudiants de Mauritanie a déclaré que le ministère de l'Enseignement supérieur et de la Recherche scientifique avait exclu les diplômés des années précédentes de la candidature à l'orientation en master, et a critiqué ce qu'elle a qualifié d'« improvisation » dans les procédures d'orientation ainsi que la réduction du nombre de spécialisations et de places disponibles dans plusieurs établissements d'enseignement supérieur. La commission d’orientation universitaire de l’Union a déclaré, dans un communiqué publié jeudi à Nouakchott, que le ministère limitait les candidatures au master aux diplômés de l’année universitaire en cours 2026, et a exigé que les candidatures soient ouvertes aux diplômés des années précédentes et que le nombre de filières et de places disponibles dans les différents établissements soit augmenté. L’Union a ajouté que la plateforme d’orientation avait connu, selon ses propres termes, des « dysfonctionnements », parmi lesquels le blocage d’étudiants brillants et l’impossibilité pour eux de classer leurs choix, alors que des étudiants n’ayant pas atteint les notes requises ont pu accéder à la plateforme et énuméré leurs choix. Le communiqué indique que la commission a également recensé des cas où des diplômés de l’année 2025 ont pu s’inscrire, alors même que l’exclusion des diplômés des années précédentes avait été annoncée, tout en critiquant l’absence d’un service dédié au traitement des réclamations et des demandes des étudiants. L’Union a demandé au ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur de mettre en place un mécanisme clair pour recevoir les recours et les réclamations, et de mettre fin à ce qu’elle a qualifié de « déni de responsabilité » envers les étudiants lésés. La fédération a également réitéré son rejet des décisions antérieures qui, selon elle, privent les meilleurs bacheliers des bourses d’études à l’étranger et les doctorants de la part officielle qui leur est allouée. L’Union a appelé les étudiants lésés et ses membres à se préparer à entreprendre des « actions de lutte » pour défendre leurs droits et leurs acquis, sans toutefois préciser la nature ni la date de ces actions.

items.title: Iran defiant on strait as Trump tells Americans to accept high gas prices
items.description: By Eman Abouhassira, Enas Alashray and Humeyra Pamuk DUBAI/CAIRO/GARDEN CITY, New York, Aug 15 (Reuters) - Iran called on the U.S. to accept defeat while President Donald Trump blasted Tehran as "very evil" and told Americans to brace for continued high fuel prices as a result of the war. Progress toward peace talks and oil tanker traffic through the strategic Strait of Hormuz waterway remained halted, with no sign the warring parties were moving toward ending the conflict that the U.S. and Israel launched on February 28.

items.title: L’agent des services de renseignement français détenus au Mali gracié suite à des bons offices du Maroc
items.description: Le ministère français des Affaires étrangères a exprimé vendredi sa « grande satisfaction » après l'annonce par le Mali de la grâce accordée à un agent des services de renseignement français qui avait été arrêté il y a environ un an et condamné à 20 ans de prison pour atteinte à la sûreté de l'État. Les médias français ont révélé que les négociations concernant la libération de Christian Bernard Vezelier avaient débuté avant son procès en juin dernier, précisant que le Maroc avait joué un rôle décisif dans cette affaire grâce à des contacts secrets avec les autorités maliennes. Radio France Internationale (RFI) a indiqué que les autorités maliennes avaient insisté pour que l’agent soit d’abord jugé avant d’envisager sa grâce ; il était le seul parmi les accusés à avoir été jugé pour « tentative de déstabilisation », tandis que les accusés maliens, dont deux généraux, sont toujours en prison. À la suite du prononcé du jugement, l’avocat de l’agent a été invité à ne pas faire appel de la décision afin de ne pas prolonger la durée de sa détention, alors que la France avait récemment menacé de fermer l’école française « Liberté » à Bamako à titre de mesure de représailles, selon une source. Les négociations se sont accélérées ces derniers temps et ont abouti à une décision de grâce et au retour de l’agent à Paris, sans que l’on sache exactement ce qu’ont obtenu les autorités maliennes en échange. Une source locale a déclaré, selon Radio France Internationale, que la partie malienne avait obtenu « beaucoup de choses », sans donner plus de détails.

items.title: Une première en Mauritanie avec l’objectif d’atteindre 500 mètres de profondeur lors de forage de puits
items.description: La Mauritanie a lancé le forage d’un puits d’exploration dont la profondeur dépasse 385 mètres près de la ville de Tintane, dans la wilaya du Hodh El Gharbi, dans le cadre d’une opération visant à atteindre plus de 500 mètres à la recherche d’eaux souterraines profondes, une initiative que la ministre de l’hydraulique et de l’Assainissement, Amal Mouloud, a qualifiée de « première du genre » dans le pays. Lors du lancement de l’opération vendredi, la ministre a indiqué que les premiers résultats du forage commençaient à apparaître et que les travaux se poursuivraient jusqu’à atteindre la profondeur visée. Elle a ajouté que cette opération était destinée à mieux connaître les réserves d’eaux souterraines profondes de la Mauritanie, ce qui contribuera à renforcer les ressources en eau et à en assurer un approvisionnement continu. Mint Mouloud a indiqué que le secteur de l’eau s’emploie à mettre en œuvre des projets d’infrastructure visant à créer de nouvelles sources d’eau, précisant que la politique du secteur prévoit la construction de grands barrages destinés au captage et au stockage. Elle a ajouté que la région du Hodh El Gharbi bénéficiera de ces infrastructures pour l’agriculture et l’élevage, ainsi que pour l’approvisionnement en eau potable, citant à cet égard le barrage de Foum Legleïta. La ministre a indiqué que le gouvernement poursuit ces efforts dans le but de fournir l’eau en quantités suffisantes et d’améliorer les services d’approvisionnement en eau.

items.title: Le festival des dattes d’Atar met l’accent sur le développement de la production, de la transformation, et sur l’ouverture de nouveaux marchés
items.description: La cinquième édition du Festival international des dattes mauritaniennes s'est ouverte vendredi à Atar, dans la région d'Adrar, en présence de producteurs, de chercheurs, d'investisseurs et d'experts, alors que le secteur du palmier dattier est confronté à des défis liés à la rareté de l'eau, au changement climatique ainsi qu'à la faiblesse de la transformation et de la commercialisation. Organisé par le ministère de l’Agriculture et de la Souveraineté alimentaire en collaboration avec le Prix international Khalifa pour le palmier dattier et l’innovation agricole, ce festival met l’accent sur le développement de la chaîne de valeur des dattes, depuis la production et la valorisation jusqu’au conditionnement, au stockage, à la transformation et à la commercialisation, ainsi que sur la promotion des investissements dans les industries liées aux dattes. Le ministre de l’élevage, Sid Ahmed Ould Mohamed, qui assure l’intérim du ministre de l’Agriculture et de la Souveraineté alimentaire, a déclaré que la culture du palmier dattier constituait un élément important du système agricole mauritanien, en particulier dans les régions oasiennes, en raison de ce qu’elle apporte en termes d’alimentation, de revenus et d’emplois, ainsi que de sa contribution à la stabilité de la population. Il a ajouté que le secteur est confronté à des défis, notamment la rareté de l’eau et le changement climatique, soulignant que les autorités s’efforcent d’améliorer la gestion des ressources en eau, d’introduire des techniques agricoles modernes et d’encourager les pratiques agricoles qui favorisent la pérennité de l’activité oasienne. Le ministre a déclaré que le festival constituait une occasion d’échanger des expériences et des techniques entre les producteurs, les chercheurs, les investisseurs et les acteurs du secteur des dattes, d’améliorer la qualité de la production et de renforcer sa compétitivité sur les marchés locaux et internationaux. L'exposition organisée en marge du festival accueille 74 stands présentant des produits à base de dattes et des dérivés du palmier, ainsi que des produits et des initiatives liés à l'agriculture oasienne. L'ambassadeur des Émirats arabes unis en Mauritanie, Hamad Ghanem Hamad Al-Mahiri, a déclaré que l'organisation de ce festival reflétait la coopération entre les deux pays dans le domaine agricole, tandis que le secrétaire général du Prix international Khalifa pour le palmier dattier et l'innovation agricole, Abdelwahab Zayed, a indiqué que le festival était devenu une plateforme d'échange de connaissances, de transfert de technologies et de développement des compétences des professionnels du secteur. La culture des palmiers dattiers constitue une activité traditionnelle dans la wilaya d’Adrar, où la saison de la récolte des dattes, connue localement sous le nom de « El Gheytana», est liée à des aspects économiques, sociaux et culturels, notamment des activités patrimoniales organisées tout au long de la saison. L’inauguration du festival a été marquée par la remise de prix à plusieurs agriculteurs et producteurs dans différentes catégories, notamment celles du meilleur producteur de différentes variétés de dattes, de la meilleure exploitation de palmiers, du meilleur produit traditionnel issu du palmier et du meilleur produit transformé ou alimentaire à base de produits du palmier. Les activités du festival se poursuivent à Atar avec la participation d’organismes, d’institutions et de producteurs de Mauritanie et d’ailleurs.

items.title: Parcelles non mises en valeur: La Direction Générale des Impôts passe à l’offensive, 10 % de pénalité et un risque de retrait
items.description: Le gouvernement burkinabè durcit le ton face à la spéculation foncière qui entrave le développement urbain. Par un communiqué officiel daté du 13 août 2026, la Directrice générale des impôts, Eliane T. Djiguemde, a annoncé la mise en œuvre effective de la taxe additionnelle applicable aux terrains non mis en valeur ou insuffisamment mis en valeur. Cette opération, qui débute par une phase pilote ciblant les parcelles de la SONATUR dans la zone de Ouaga 2000, marque un tournant décisif : au-delà des pénalités financières, les propriétaires récalcitrants s'exposent désormais au retrait pur et simple de leurs parcelles au profit du domaine foncier de l'État. L'heure est à la mise en valeur pour les propriétaires fonciers de la capitale. La Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) vient d'activer un levier fiscal longtemps attendu pour lutter contre la rétention spéculative des parcelles : la taxe additionnelle, prévue par les articles 279-2 et suivants du Code général des impôts. Ouaga 2000 : Le point de départ d'une réforme nationale L'opération ne sera pas globale d’emblée, mais procédera par étapes géographiques. Pour cette première phase, le viseur des impôts est braqué sur la région du Kadiogo, et plus particulièrement sur la zone de Ouaga 2000. Les services de la DGI ont déjà procédé, depuis juillet 2024, à des opérations de constat pour identifier les terrains restés à l'état de broussailles ou insuffisamment aménagés au regard des normes d'urbanisme. Les parcelles concernées sont principalement celles aménagées par la Société nationale d’aménagement des terrains urbains (SONATUR). Les propriétaires concernés sont invités à retirer leurs avis d'imposition tous les jours ouvrables, de 8 heures à 15 heures, soit à la Direction du centre des impôts de Ouaga VIII, soit au Centre départemental des impôts de Komsilga. Pour faciliter les démarches, la DGI a mis en place une plateforme de consultation en ligne à l’adresse https://etitre2.dgi.bf , permettant à chacun de vérifier le montant dû. Le calendrier imposé par l'administration fiscale est rigoureux. Une fois l'avis d'imposition réputé délivré (soit un mois après la diffusion du communiqué), le titulaire dispose de deux mois pour s'acquitter de la taxe. Passé ce délai, un sursis de trois mois est accordé, mais il s'accompagne d'une pénalité de 10 %. C'est ici que la mesure devient réellement dissuasive : si à l'expiration de ce sursis le paiement n'est toujours pas effectué, la loi prévoit le retrait de la parcelle. Le terrain est alors réincorporé d'office dans le domaine foncier de l’État, une mesure radicale qui vise à favoriser une gestion rationnelle de l'espace national et à encourager la construction effective de logements. À travers ce tour de vis fiscal, la Directrice générale des impôts, Eliane T. Djiguemde, entend non seulement renflouer les caisses de l'État, mais surtout envoyer un signal fort aux spéculateurs : la terre n'est plus un simple placement passif, elle doit désormais servir à bâtir l'avenir des villes burkinabè. L’article Parcelles non mises en valeur: La Direction Générale des Impôts passe à l'offensive, 10 % de pénalité et un risque de retrait est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: La police démantèle un réseau de trafiquants de drogue et procède à l’arrestation de 11 suspects
